bull_bear.body:
- India's leading manufacturer of winding wires and strips; among India's largest copper tube manufacturing operations
- Ability to manufacture across one of the widest dimensional ranges in the industry (5 mm to 0.016 mm), a capability among limited organised players in India
- Preferred supplier to leading OEMs (Cummins, Siemens, CG Power, Schneider Electric, Havells, Godrej & Boyce, Amber Enterprises, Epack Durables, Daikin, Panasonic Life Solutions, Bosch), driving ~70-75% of business
- Robust pan-India distribution network
- Diversified portfolio across many product lines so strength is not tied to a single product or plant
- Vertically integrated, technology-driven manufacturing with automation, integrated quality monitoring and Eddy Current Testing
- Copper tubes localisation / import-substitution positioning in a segment historically dependent on imports
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Copper raw-material intensity and price volatility — Efficient use of raw materials, particularly copper, is critical for the resource-intensive winding-wire and copper-tube operations; inefficient consumption directly erodes margins and strains supply resilience.
- Energy cost and emissions exposure — Energy consumption remains a major driver of manufacturing costs, and efficiency investments are needed to stay aligned with evolving environmental regulations and climate commitments.
- Occupational health and safety in manufacturing — Manufacturing operations inherently carry workplace risks; strong safety systems are essential for workforce protection and statutory compliance, with failures risking legal and financial penalties.
- Supply-chain / vendor ESG risk — The supply chain is a significant source of indirect environmental and social impact; vendor failure to adhere to ESG standards can cause supply disruptions, reputational damage, and financial penalties.
- Regulatory compliance across environmental, labour and corporate rules — Operations are subject to varied environmental, labour and corporate regulations; lapses can cause business disruptions and fines, requiring proactive compliance monitoring.
- Demand concentration / market cyclicality — Exposure to demand fluctuations and geographic-sector concentration; the Company pursues market diversification across geographies and sectors (EV, renewable energy) and export expansion to reduce this risk.
- Commoditisation and margin pressure in standard products — Reliance on commoditised wire products invites competitive pressure; a strategic shift toward higher-margin value-added products (paper magnet wires, ultrafine copper wires) is being pursued to defend profitability.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Ram Ratna Wires, operating since 1992, manufactures copper and aluminium winding wires and strips across one of the industry's widest dimensional ranges (from 5 mm down to ultra-fine 0.016 mm), serving India's electrical ecosystem. It has expanded beyond winding wires into specialised conductors, value-added electrical solutions and seamless copper tubes (via the Bhiwadi facility and merged Global Copper), positioning itself as an integrated copper products platform. It supplies leading OEMs across automotive, industrial, HVAC and electronics, with OEM customers driving roughly 70-75% of business.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Winding wires & strips:** Enamelled copper wire and strips, Enamelled aluminium wires and strips, Submersible winding wires, Multi-layered submersible winding wires, Fiber glass covered copper and aluminium strips, Paper cover round wires, Super fine wires (down to 0.016 mm), Advanced litz wires, Kapton-covered litz wires (EV charging), MCB coils of enamelled strips, Parallel wires for EV hub motor windings
- **Copper tubes & pipes:** Level Wound Coils (LWC), Inner Grooved Tubes (IGT), Pancake Coils (PCC), Straight copper tubes, Capillary tubes, PVC-coated tubes, Specialised industrial copper tube solutions
business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- Tefabo Product Pvt. Ltd. (TPPL) — subsidiary: 64% owned (raised via acquisition of an additional 4% equity during the year); manufactures fabricated components and assemblies for the renewable energy sector, strengthening the parent's green energy portfolio
- Epavo Electricals Limited — JV: Joint venture of the parent and Epack Durable Limited; manufactures BLDC motors for air conditioners, HVLS fans, submersible pumps and related products
- RR-Imperial Electricals Limited — JV: Jointly Controlled Entity incorporated and operating in Bangladesh; mixed product portfolio of wires and cables
- Epack Durable Limited — JV: Joint-venture partner alongside the parent in Epavo Electricals Limited

outlook.body:
- Reinvestment-led: the Company funds capacity expansion (new Bhiwadi copper-tube facility under the PLI scheme, taking it to five manufacturing plants) and its green-energy portfolio (raising its stake in subsidiary Tefabo Product Pvt. Ltd. to 64%). Members approved enhancing the Section 180(1)(c) borrowing limit to Rs 1,500 crores (from Rs 1,200 crores) to support business needs, with corresponding enhancement of the Section 180(1)(a) charge-creation limit. The Company accepts no public deposits, and unclaimed dividends/shares are transferred to the IEPF per statute. No buyback, sweat-equity or differential-rights issuance during the year.
- Resource efficiency: implement lean manufacturing and invest in advanced machinery to minimise waste and process scrap, reducing copper/raw-material consumption
- Energy and emissions: adopt renewable energy, replace inefficient machines, conduct regular energy audits, and use catalytic enamelling machines to minimise emissions
- Occupational health and safety: mandatory safety training, regular drills, ISO 45001 certification processes, and incident-reporting systems
- Vendor ESG: transition from standard contractual purchase-order clauses to a structured vendor ESG assessment framework with verification mechanisms
- Value-added product portfolio: increase R&D investment and technology-transfer partnerships to shift toward higher-margin, innovation-led products (e.g., paper magnet wires, ultrafine copper wires)
- Regulatory compliance: deploy robust compliance monitoring systems, regular legal audits, and active engagement with regulatory bodies
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: During FY2025-26 Ram Ratna Wires pursued inorganic expansion and structural consolidation; the routed capex sections disclose no greenfield plant/line capacity-addition project with a commissioning timeline. The NCLT (Mumbai Bench) sanctioned the merger by absorption of Global Copper Private Limited - described as a material unlisted subsidiary - into the Company (order dated May 29, 2025; Scheme effective June 23, 2025 on filing with the RoC; appointed date April 01, 2024), integrating the copper business into the parent. The Company completed acquisition of an additional 4% stake in its subsidiary Tefabo Product Private Limited (registered office in Bangalore), raising its holding from 60% to 64%. It retains two joint venture companies - Epavo Electricals Private Limited (Maharashtra) and RR-Imperial Electricals Limited (based in Bangladesh). To support future funding needs, members were asked (Special Resolution at the AGM) to enhance the Section 180(1)(c) borrowing limit from Rs 1,200 crores to Rs 1,500 crores. Capital-structure actions during the year included a 1:1 bonus issue and an increase in authorized share capital from Rs 25 crores to Rs 50 crores.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans
